title: Congressional Testimony by Nelson Gross on International Narcotics Control
relevant_claim: U.S. country teams coordinated foreign narcotics plans and built enforcement and intelligence capability
quote_or_summary: Interagency committees included State AID BNDD Customs Defense CIA and USIA; missions prepared more than 50 action plans
notes: Primary official synthesis

title: Laos narcotics-control origin
relevant_claim: The Lao program followed Vientiane-origin heroin seizures at Tan Son Nhut
quote_or_summary: Mission encouragement produced a Lao program; BNDD intelligence led to a dealer arrest with 10 kilograms
notes: Official account may emphasize program success

title: U-Tapao forged-document shipment
relevant_entity: Andrew Price; William Henry Jackson; Jerald Ganius
relevant_claim: A 17-pound heroin shipment moved via U-Tapao using forged military documents
quote_or_summary: Arrests followed months of Thai police and BNDD investigation
notes: Underlying case file not acquired

title: Golden Triangle narcotics routes
relevant_claim: CIA analysis mapped regional processing and onward routes
quote_or_summary: Opium and morphine base moved toward processing and international markets
notes: Analytical estimate rather than shipment case

title: The Politics of Heroin in Southeast Asia
relevant_claim: Trafficante was an organized-crime narcotics financier and traveled to Asia in 1968
quote_or_summary: McCoy frames the trip as a search for alternate supply
notes: Travel rests partly on Senate record; purpose is inference

title: Alleged Assassination Plots Involving Foreign Leaders
relevant_claim: CIA intermediaries worked with Trafficante in Castro assassination plotting
quote_or_summary: The committee documented meetings and poison-plot activity
notes: Proves CIA relationship unrelated to heroin

title: Report re Santo Trafficante Jr. MM 92-88
relevant_claim: Federal investigation reportedly found no evidence of a narcotics conspiracy behind the 1968 trip
quote_or_summary: Original file is indexed as NARA record 124-10213-10207
notes: Human review required; current finding traced through Marshall

title: Dirty Wars: French and American Piaster Profiteering in Indochina 1945-75
relevant_claim: FBI investigation weakens the narcotics-purpose interpretation of Trafficante's trip
quote_or_summary: Marshall cites FBI and Senate files and says officials found no supporting evidence
notes: Best located synthesis of primary counterevidence

title: Corsican networks in Saigon and Vientiane
relevant_claim: Conein described Vientiane-Saigon-Marseille family and shipping links
quote_or_summary: Morphine base allegedly moved through Corsican contacts and French merchant vessels
notes: Underlying interview notes not acquired

title: Lansdale Corsican truce
relevant_claim: Lansdale said he made a truce and was not conducting criminal investigations
quote_or_summary: He later knew of narcotics activity and took no action because it was outside his mission
notes: Supports mission-priority tolerance; not a trafficking partnership

title: McCoy testimony before Senator Proxmire's committee
relevant_claim: McCoy named Theodas as the alleged arranger of Sopsaisana's French connection
quote_or_summary: McCoy attributed the claim to BNDD and diplomatic sources
notes: Underlying BNDD record not acquired

title: Search and Destroy—The War on Drugs
relevant_claim: Contemporary reporting corroborates an Orly heroin seizure and refusal of credentials
quote_or_summary: A valise contained about 123 pounds of heroin
notes: Does not establish supplier recipient or onward route

title: Sopsaisana affair
relevant_claim: McCoy's diplomatic and BNDD sources alleged a Long Tieng origin and Corsican destination
quote_or_summary: Sopsaisana denied ownership and claimed a frame-up
notes: Bulk seizure stronger than alleged upstream chain

title: Fiscal Year 1976 Program Guidance Airgram A-102
relevant_claim: Program was deliberately limited and scaled down from about 30 U.S. personnel to 10
quote_or_summary: Program peaked near $2 million in 1973 and trained 711 Lao enforcement/judicial personnel
notes: Strong program-scale record

title: Royal Lao Military Police narcotics program
relevant_claim: 163 military police had initial training and seven had U.S. narcotics training
quote_or_summary: Objective addressed RLA-official trafficking and military transportation; checkpoints were planned
notes: Seven officers remain unidentified

title: GSI and DEA transition
relevant_claim: OPS assistance was scheduled to end and DEA to assume narcotics advising
quote_or_summary: GSI combined personnel detailed from police military police and Customs
notes: Shows functional handoff not institutional identity

title: Police Academy Review vol. 9 no. 1
relevant_claim: PMNO No. 8 had 27 classmates from nine countries including Laos and Thailand
quote_or_summary: IPA reported 5204 graduates from 77 countries
notes: No full student roster in issue

title: Federal Law Enforcement and Criminal Justice Activities FY1971
relevant_claim: OPS built whole-force narcotics capacity and IPA alumni served as DOJ contacts
quote_or_summary: 3932 graduates from 73 countries; 13 national agencies commanded by graduates
notes: Agencies and chiefs not named

title: Annual Report of the Secretary of the Treasury FY1966
relevant_claim: FBN taught a two-week Spanish-language narcotics course for 19 Latin American officers
quote_or_summary: Covered cocaine heroin and marijuana
notes: First of three consecutive annual reports

title: Annual Report of the Secretary of the Treasury FY1967
relevant_claim: FBN continued two-week narcotics-control instruction with IPA/AID
quote_or_summary: Documents institutional continuity
notes: Do not transfer 1966 cohort count

title: Annual Report of the Secretary of the Treasury FY1968
relevant_claim: Bilingual FBN agents again taught narcotics control at IPA
quote_or_summary: Third consecutive official report
notes: Aggregate institutional evidence

title: Project TWO-FOLD
relevant_claim: CIA spotted assessed and recruited BNDD internal-security personnel and covert staff agents
quote_or_summary: Recruits became BNDD employees and were unaware of CIA administrative involvement
notes: Strongest proof of CIA access inside narcotics enforcement

title: Origins of CIA assistance to BNDD
relevant_claim: Ingersoll sought CIA help because he believed old FBN corruption was tied to smuggling interests
quote_or_summary: DCI approved covert recruitment assistance
notes: Does not identify corrupt individuals

title: Narrowing Project TWO-FOLD
relevant_claim: Domestic internal-corruption support was terminated while foreign narcotics-intelligence staffing continued
quote_or_summary: Foreign branch was directed against international traffickers
notes: Subsequent operations and countries not located

title: Larger CIA Role in International Narcotics Matters
relevant_claim: CIA was pressed to lead expanded collection on international trafficking systems
quote_or_summary: CIA coordinated the CCINC Intelligence Subcommittee
notes: Evidence of collection role not enforcement command

title: Tachilek refinery ownership
relevant_entity: Law Sik Han; Yang Sun; KKY
relevant_claim: Private KKY/Shan militia refineries operated around Tachilek
quote_or_summary: Law Sik Han and other militia actors had refinery routes; CIA estimated fourteen area labs
notes: Supports competitive-effect inference only

title: CIF proposal against Tachilek refineries
relevant_claim: U.S. officials considered covertly using opium-financed CIF forces against heroin refineries
quote_or_summary: American role was to remain concealed
notes: Document does not identify refinery owners or commercial motive

title: Foreign Assistance Act of 1974 Public Law 93-559
relevant_claim: Broad police-assistance ban took effect July 1 1975 with narcotics and specified DEA/FBI exceptions
quote_or_summary: International narcotics exception existed at enactment
notes: Enactment and effective date differ

title: Stopping U.S. Assistance to Foreign Police and Prisons
relevant_claim: The 1973 act had already triggered phaseout of 17 programs and 95 advisers
quote_or_summary: GAO found general compliance and growing narcotics aid
notes: Official implementation review

title: International Security and Development Cooperation Act of 1985 Public Law 99-83
relevant_claim: Later law added judicial investigative and country exceptions
quote_or_summary: Later exceptions must not be projected backward
notes: Relevant only to chronology
